title: T-cell tailored single-cell RNA barcoding and sequencing (tSCRB-seq)
protocol: Decontaminate all contact surfaces with RNaseZap.
Prepare 96-well low-binding plates for single-cell sorting by dispensing 10 µl of Qiagen TCL buffer supplemented with 1% 2-mercaptoethanol per well.
Seal the plates well with adhesive foil.
Store the sealed plates at room temperature for up to one day.
Do not store the plates for prolonged periods to avoid lysis evaporation.
Using large nozzle size (100 µm) and single-cell purity mode, sort a single cell of interest into each well of the PCR plate.
Before sorting the population of interest, test the correct aiming of the machine.
Sort 10-20 cells per well into few wells located on top and bottom of a sealed with transparent seal PCR plate.
The droplets should be visible on the seal surface.
Sort 10-20 cells per well into few wells located on top and bottom of an empty PCR plate.
The liquid droplet should be visible at the bottom of the PCR plate.
Do not use smaller than 100 µm nozzle to avoid unnecessary cell stress.
Seal the plate with adhesive foil immediately after sorting.
Spin the sealed plate down for 30 seconds at 1000 rcf.
Snap-freeze the spun-down plate using dry ice.
Transfer the plates to a -80°C freezer for storage.
Decontaminate all contact surfaces with RNaseZap.
Equilibrate RNAClean XP beads at room temperature (~2300 ml per plate).
Prepare fresh 80% molecular grade ethanol (~40 ml per plate).
Thaw and keep the 5 x Maxima H-Buffer on ice.
Thaw and keep the Advantage dNTP Mix on ice.
Thaw and keep the SCRB-seq Template Switching Oligo on ice.
Thaw and keep the tSCRB Barcoded Oligo-dT Primer Plate v3 on ice.
Prepare reverse transcription component 1 (RT c1) according to Table 1 instructions.
Dispense the required amount of RT c1 into each well of a 0.2 ml 8-tube strip with attached caps.
Prepare reverse transcription component 3 (RT c3) according to Table 2 instructions.
Dispense the required amount of RT c3 into each well of a 0.2 ml 8-tube strip with attached caps.
Thaw a frozen PCR plate with single cells.
Vortex the thawed PCR plate for 5 seconds and spin down at 1000 rcf for 30 seconds.
Vortex RNAClean XP beads until fully resuspended.
Dispense RNAClean XP beads into a 25 ml reagent reservoir.
Add 22 µl of RNAClean XP beads to each well of the single-cell plate using a multichannel pipette.
Gently pipette each well 15 times to mix.
Cover the plate to prevent contamination from dust and incubate for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Place the plate on the magnetic separator and incubate until the solution is clear.
Without disturbing the ring of separated magnetic beads, aspirate and discard 20 µl of the supernatant.
Add 180 µl of 80% molecular grade ethanol to each well.
If the beads are not collected in a compact ring, move the plate gently up and down on the magnetic stand to collect them.
Incubate for 30 seconds at room temperature.
Without disturbing the ring of separated magnetic beads, remove the supernatant completely.
Add 180 μl of 80% molecular grade ethanol to each well.
Incubate for 30 seconds.
Remove the supernatant completely without disturbing the ring of separated magnetic beads.
Gently tap the magnetic stand with the plate on it to remove any residual liquid droplets from the walls.
Aspirate the residual volume of liquid with 10 μl tips loaded on a multichannel pipette.
Remove the PCR plate from the magnetic stand.
Add 2.8 μl of RT component 1 to each well of the single-cell plate using a multichannel pipette and mix thoroughly.
Add 1.2 μl of the respective barcoded primer from the stock 14 µM tSCRB Barcoded Oligo-dT Primer Plate v3 to each well of the single-cell plate using a multichannel pipette and mix.
Spin the stock primer plate for 30 seconds at 1000 rcf.
Incubate the single-cell plate on a thermal cycler with heated lid at 105°C for 3 minutes and forever at 4°C.
Seal the single-cell plate with adhesive foil.
Spin the single-cell plate for 30 seconds at 1000 rcf to collect liquid at the bottom of the wells.
Add 3 μl of reverse transcription component 3 (RT c3) to each well of the single-cell plate using a multichannel pipette.
Mix after adding RT c3.
Seal the single-cell plate with adhesive foil.
Spin the single-cell plate for 30 seconds at 1000 rcf to collect liquid at the bottom of the wells.
Incubate the plate on a thermal cycler using the following program: heated lid at 105°C, 90 minutes at 42°C, 15 minutes at 72°C, hold at 4°C.
Thaw and keep the KAPA HiFi HotStart ReadyMix and SCRB SMART PCR primer on ice.
Prepare the PCR master mix shortly before the incubation ends.
Spin the single-cell plate for 30 seconds at 1000 rcf to collect the liquid at the bottom of the wells.
Dispense the necessary amount of PCR master mix in a 25 ml reagent reservoir.
Using a multichannel pipette, add 18 μl of PCR master to each well of the single-cell plate and mix.
Seal the single-cell plate with adhesive foil.
Spin the single-cell plate for 30 seconds at 1000 rcf to collect the liquid at the bottom of the wells.
Incubate the plate on a thermal cycler with heated lid at 100°C for 3 minutes.
Perform 18 to 20 cycles of incubation: 20 seconds at 98°C, 30 seconds at 65°C, and 6 minutes at 72°C.
Incubate for an additional 5 minutes at 72°C.
Hold the plate at 4°C after cycling.
Equilibrate AMPure XP beads at room temperature (~1500 ml per plate).
Prepare fresh 80% molecular grade ethanol (~12 ml per plate).
Spin the single-cell plate for 30 seconds at 1000 rcf to collect liquid in the wells.
Collect barcoded single-cell transcriptomes from one plate into two 2.0 ml DNA LoBind Tubes: columns 1-6 into one tube, and columns 7-12 into another tube.
Vortex AMPure XP beads until fully resuspended.
Add 870 μl of AMPure XP beads to each tube and gently pipette 15 times to mix.
Incubate for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Place the tubes on the magnetic separator and incubate until the solution is clear.
Without disturbing the ring of separated magnetic beads, aspirate and discard the supernatant.
Add 2 ml of 80% molecular grade ethanol to each tube. Incubate for 30 seconds.
Without disturbing the ring of separated magnetic beads, aspirate and discard the supernatant.
Add 2 ml of 80% molecular grade ethanol to each tube. Incubate for 30 seconds.
Without disturbing the ring of separated magnetic beads, aspirate and discard the supernatant.
Remove any residual liquid droplets from the walls by gently tapping the magnetic stand with the tubes on it to the bench surface.
Aspirate the residual volume of liquid using a 10 μl tip.
Allow the ethanol to evaporate from the tubes until the ring of separate magnetic beads loses its glossiness.
Remove the tubes from the magnetic separator and resuspend the beads in 30 μl molecular grade water.
Combine the content of two tubes from one plate into a single tube and incubate for 2 minutes at room temperature.
Place the tube(s) on the magnetic separator and wait until the solution is clear.
Transfer 55 μl of supernatant into a well of a PCR plate without disturbing the beads.
Vortex the AMPure XP beads until fully resuspended. Add 33 µl to each used well in the PCR plate, mix gently by pipetting 15 times, and cover the plate.
Incubate the covered plate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Place the plate on the magnetic separator and wait until the solution is clear.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant without disturbing the ring of separated beads.
Add 180 µl of 80% molecular grade ethanol to each used well from the PCR plate.
Incubate for 30 seconds.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant without disturbing the ring of separated magnetic beads.
Add 180 µl of 80% molecular grade ethanol to each used well from the PCR plate. Incubate for 30 seconds.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant without disturbing the ring of separated magnetic beads.
Gently tap the magnetic stand with the plate to remove any residual liquid droplets from the walls.
Aspirate the residual volume using 10 µl tips.
Allow the ethanol to evaporate until the ring of separate magnetic beads loses its glossiness (about 2 minutes).
Resuspend the beads in 10-30 μl molecular grade water. Incubate for 2 minutes at room temperature.
Place the plate on the magnetic separator and incubate until the solution is clear.
Transfer 9-28 µl of the supernatant into a 1.5 ml DNA LoBind Tube without disturbing the ring of separated magnetic beads.
Run 1 µl of each elute on a Bionalyzer High Sensitivity chip for band quality control and quantification.
Thaw Tagment DNA Buffer (TD buffer) and keep it on ice.
Keep Amplicon Tagment Mix (ATM) on ice.
Keep Nextera PCR Master Mix (NPM) on ice.
Keep 10 µM SCRB-seq custom N5 primer on ice.
Keep 10 µM Nextera P7 index primers on ice.
Dilute 1 ng of amplicon from each single-cell plate to a volume of 5 μl in a well of a PCR plate.
Add 10 µl TD buffer to each used well of the PCR plate.
Add 5 µl ATM to each used well of the PCR plate.
Using a multichannel pipette set to 15 µl, gently mix the reaction 10 times.
Seal the PCR plate with a transparent seal.
Spin the plate for 30 seconds at 1000 rcf to collect the liquid at the bottom of the wells.
Incubate the plate on a thermal cycler using the following program: heated lid at 100°C, 5 minutes at 55°C, hold at 4°C.
Immediately after incubation, add 5 μl Neutralize Tagment Buffer (NT buffer) to each used well of the PCR plate and gently mix 10 times.
Cover the plate to prevent dust contamination and incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Add 15 μl NPM and 8 μl molecular grade water to each used well of the PCR plate.
Add 1 μl of the 10 μM SCRB-seq custom N5 primer to each used well of the PCR plate.
Add 1 μl of the respective indexing 10 μM Nextera P7 primer to each sample.
Using a multichannel pipette set to 30 μl, gently mix the reaction 10 times.
Seal the PCR plate with a transparent seal.
Spin the plate for 30 seconds at 1000 rcf to collect the liquid at the bottom of the wells.
Incubate the plate on a thermal cycler with heated lid at 100°C for 3 minutes.
Incubate the plate for 30 seconds at 95°C.
Repeat 12 cycles: incubate for 10 seconds at 95°C, then for 30 seconds at 55°C, followed by 30 seconds at 72°C.
Incubate the plate for 5 minutes at 72°C.
Hold the plate at 10°C.
Equilibrate the AMPure XP beads at room temperature (~60 μl per sample).
Prepare fresh 80% molecular grade ethanol (~800 μl per sample).
Spin the plate for 30 seconds at 1000 rcf to collect liquid at the bottom of wells.
Vortex the AMPure XP beads until fully resuspended.
Add 30 µl of AMPure XP beads to each used well of the PCR plate and gently pipette 15 times to mix. Cover the plate to prevent contamination from dust.
Incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Place the plate on the magnetic separator and incubate until the solution is clear.
Without disturbing the ring of separated magnetic beads, aspirate and discard the supernatant.
Add 180 µl of 80% molecular grade ethanol to each used well from the PCR plate.
Incubate for 30 seconds.
Without disturbing the ring of separated magnetic beads, aspirate and discard the supernatant.
Add 180 µl of 80% molecular grade ethanol to each used well from the PCR plate.
Incubate for 30 seconds.
Without disturbing the ring of separated magnetic beads, aspirate and discard the supernatant.
Remove any residual liquid droplets from the walls by gently tapping the magnetic stand with the plate to the bench surface.
Aspirate the residual volume of liquid using 10 µl tips.
Allow the ethanol to evaporate from the wells until the ring of separate magnetic beads loses its glossiness (about 2 minutes).
Remove the plate from the magnetic separator and resuspend the beads from each well in 52 μl molecular grade water.
Incubate for 2 minutes at room temperature.
Place the plate on the magnetic separator and incubate until the solution is clear.
Without disturbing the ring of separated magnetic beads, transfer 50 µl of the supernatant into a well of a new PCR plate.
Vortex the AMPure XP beads until fully resuspended.
Add 30 µl of AMPure XP beads to each used well of the new PCR plate and gently pipette 15 times to mix.
Cover the plate to prevent contamination from dust and incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Place the plate on the magnetic separator and incubate until the solution is clear.
Without disturbing the ring of separated magnetic beads, aspirate and discard the supernatant.
Add 180 µl of 80% molecular grade ethanol to each used well from the PCR plate. Incubate for 30 seconds.
Without disturbing the ring of separated magnetic beads, aspirate and discard the supernatant.
Add 180 µl of 80% molecular grade ethanol to each used well from the PCR plate. Incubate for 30 seconds.
Without disturbing the ring of separated magnetic beads, aspirate and discard the supernatant.
Remove any residual liquid droplets from the walls by gently tapping the magnetic stand with the plate to the bench surface.
Aspirate the residual volume of liquid using 10 µl tips.
Allow the ethanol to evaporate from the wells until the ring of separate magnetic beads loses its glossiness (about 2 minutes).
Remove the plate from the magnetic separator.
Resuspend the beads from each well in 10 μl molecular grade water.
Incubate the resuspended beads for 2 minutes at room temperature.
Place the plate on the magnetic separator and incubate until the solution is clear.
Without disturbing the ring of separated magnetic beads, transfer 9 μl of the supernatant into a PCR tube.
Run 1 μl of each elute on a Bionalyzer High Sensitivity chip for band quality control.
